name: Pieter Abbeel
title: Professor, Jim Gray Chair of Engineering
research_summary: Directs the Berkeley Robot Learning Lab and co-directs BAIR, pioneering deep reinforcement learning and apprenticeship learning for teaching robots complex skills from human demonstrations. Co-founded Covariant (AI-powered industrial robotics) and Gradescope, and his foundational work on learning from human feedback directly underpins modern RLHF methods used in LLM alignment.

papers.title: Learning to Learn with Gradients (MAML)
papers.one_line_summary: Introduces Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning, training models to adapt to new tasks in just a few gradient steps by optimizing for fast adaptation rather than task-specific performance. Became one of the most cited meta-learning papers, enabling few-shot learning across robotics, vision, and NLP.

papers.title: Apprenticeship Learning via Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.one_line_summary: Proposes learning reward functions directly from expert demonstrations rather than hand-engineering them, allowing agents to match expert behavior on complex tasks. Established inverse reinforcement learning as a practical approach to imitation learning in robotics and autonomous systems.

papers.title: Autonomous Helicopter Aerobatics through Apprenticeship Learning
papers.one_line_summary: Demonstrates that a helicopter can learn to perform advanced aerobatic maneuvers by observing a human pilot, using apprenticeship learning to infer the reward structure behind expert behavior. Showed that IRL-based approaches can match or exceed human expert performance on physically demanding real-world control tasks.

name: Krste Asanović
title: Professor Emeritus, Professor of the Graduate School
research_summary: Co-creator of the RISC-V open instruction set architecture and co-founder of SiFive, leading research on agile hardware design methodologies and specialized computing ecosystems at Berkeley. Directs the SLICE lab, developing open-source tools like Chipyard, FireSim, and the Gemmini ML accelerator generator that are now widely used across academia and industry.

papers.title: The RISC-V Instruction Set Manual
papers.one_line_summary: Defines the RISC-V free and open ISA originally developed at UC Berkeley, designed to support a wide range of implementations from embedded microcontrollers to warehouse-scale computers. RISC-V has since become one of the most widely adopted open ISAs in history, with billions of chips shipped and adoption by Google, NVIDIA, and Western Digital.

papers.title: Gemmini: Enabling Systematic Deep-Learning Architecture Evaluation via Full-Stack Integration
papers.one_line_summary: Presents Gemmini, an open-source systolic-array ML accelerator generator that produces full hardware-software stacks for evaluating neural network accelerator designs. Enables researchers to explore the entire design space from chip architecture to compiler and OS integration within a unified Chipyard framework.

papers.title: FireSim: FPGA-Accelerated Cycle-Exact Scale-Out System Simulation in the Public Cloud
papers.one_line_summary: Introduces FireSim, a platform that runs cycle-accurate RTL simulations of complete datacenter-scale systems on cloud FPGAs at speeds 100x faster than software simulators. Enables researchers to simulate thousands of servers running real software stacks, making previously intractable architecture research experiments feasible.

name: Ruzena Bajcsy
title: Professor Emeritus, EECS
research_summary: Pioneered the concept of 'active perception' — the idea that perception is an active, goal-directed process rather than passive image processing — which became foundational to modern robotics and computer vision. Directs the Tele-immersion Lab at Berkeley, developing 3D telepresence systems for remote collaboration, rehabilitation, and healthcare monitoring using depth cameras and sensor networks.

papers.title: Active Perception
papers.one_line_summary: Introduced the paradigm of active perception, arguing that intelligent systems should control their sensors to gather task-relevant information rather than passively processing whatever data arrives. This foundational paper directly influenced decades of work in robotics, computer vision, and autonomous systems by reframing perception as a purposeful, action-driven process.

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of an Interactive Exercise Coaching System for Older Adults
papers.one_line_summary: Presents a Kinect-based system that monitors and coaches elderly users through physical therapy exercises at home, providing real-time feedback without requiring clinical supervision. Demonstrates that depth-sensor-based motion analysis can reliably assess exercise quality and reduce barriers to rehabilitation for aging populations.

papers.title: Semi-Autonomous Vehicular Control Using Driver Modeling
papers.one_line_summary: Develops a probabilistic model of driver intent and behavior that enables a vehicle to smoothly share control between human and autonomous systems based on inferred driver goals. Shows that intent-aware shared autonomy reduces intervention conflicts and improves safety compared to threshold-based takeover systems.

name: David Bamman
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Applies NLP and AI to empirical questions in the humanities and social sciences, building specialized tools like BookNLP and LitBank for processing literary texts at scale. His lab studies representation and bias in literature, film, and culture — including measuring diversity in Hollywood, tracking gender in fiction, and auditing what large language models like GPT-4 have memorized from books.

papers.title: Measuring Diversity in Hollywood through the Large-Scale Computational Analysis of Film
papers.one_line_summary: Uses computer vision and NLP to quantify gender and racial representation across thousands of Hollywood films, revealing systematic disparities in screen time, dialogue, and character roles. Published in PNAS, demonstrating how computational methods can make large-scale diversity audits reproducible and scalable across entire film archives.

papers.title: Speak, Memory: An Archaeology of Books Known to ChatGPT/GPT-4
papers.one_line_summary: Develops a method to empirically measure which books GPT-4 has memorized from training data by probing the model with masked passages and analyzing its completions. Finds that GPT-4 has significantly more knowledge of books that are likely in its training set, raising important questions about copyright and the opacity of LLM training data.

papers.title: On Classification with Large Language Models in Cultural Analytics
papers.one_line_summary: Systematically evaluates the reliability of LLMs for classification tasks in cultural analytics, identifying failure modes when applying general-purpose models to literary and historical texts. Argues that domain-specific evaluation frameworks are essential rather than assuming general benchmark performance transfers to humanistic applications.

name: Peter Bartlett
title: Professor
research_summary: Directs the Collaboration on the Theoretical Foundations of Deep Learning and the Foundations of Data Science Institute at Berkeley, developing mathematical theory that explains why overparameterized deep networks generalize well despite fitting noisy training data exactly. His work establishes fundamental complexity bounds, convergence guarantees, and statistical limits that underpin modern understanding of deep learning and reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Benign Overfitting in Linear Regression
papers.one_line_summary: Proves mathematically that interpolating models — those that perfectly fit noisy training data — can still generalize well under specific conditions on the data distribution, overturning the classical bias-variance tradeoff intuition. This result became foundational for understanding why massively overparameterized deep neural networks work in practice despite fitting training data exactly.

papers.title: Nearly-tight VC-dimension and Pseudodimension Bounds for Piecewise Linear Neural Networks
papers.one_line_summary: Establishes tight upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension of deep ReLU networks as a function of depth and width, precisely characterizing their expressive capacity. These bounds are essential for understanding the sample complexity of learning with deep networks and form a cornerstone of modern neural network theory.

papers.title: Spectrally-normalized Margin Bounds for Neural Networks
papers.one_line_summary: Derives generalization bounds for deep networks based on the spectral norms of weight matrices rather than the total number of parameters, explaining why large neural networks can generalize despite having far more parameters than training examples. Introduced a practical framework for measuring the complexity of neural networks that connects theoretical bounds to empirical performance.

name: Aayushi Shrivastava
title: PhD Student, Mechanical Engineering
research_summary: PhD student at the ICON Lab at Berkeley combining machine learning and control theory to develop safe motion planning algorithms for highly dynamic robots. Her work focuses on provably safe control policies for hybrid dynamical systems and multi-terrain locomotion for bipedal robots.

papers.title: Demonstrating a Robust Walking Algorithm for Underactuated Bipedal Robots in Non-flat, Non-stationary Environments
papers.one_line_summary: Presents a walking controller for bipedal robots that remains stable across uneven, moving terrain without requiring flat or stationary ground assumptions. Demonstrated on hardware at IROS 2024, showing the algorithm's robustness to real-world surface variations that typically cause bipedal robots to fall.

papers.title: Stair Climbing using the Angular Momentum Linear Inverted Pendulum Model and Model Predictive Control
papers.one_line_summary: Develops a stair-climbing controller for bipedal robots using the Angular Momentum Linear Inverted Pendulum model combined with Model Predictive Control to plan stable footstep trajectories in real time. Demonstrates reliable stair ascent and descent on hardware, a challenging task for underactuated bipedal systems.

papers.title: Learning Control Policies to Provably Satisfy Hard Affine Constraints for Black-Box Hybrid Dynamical Systems
papers.one_line_summary: Proposes a learning-based method for synthesizing control policies that are guaranteed to satisfy hard safety constraints for hybrid dynamical systems whose dynamics are not fully known. Addresses a key open problem in safe reinforcement learning where formal safety guarantees are needed even when the system model is a black box.

name: Alan Zhu
title: PhD Student, Computer Science
research_summary: Second-year CS PhD student at Berkeley advised by Prof. Joseph Gonzalez, working on data-efficient methods for adapting AI systems to new domains with minimal data. His current focus is LLM personalization from limited user interactions and benchmarking how well AI agents adapt to complex social environments.

papers.title: How to Train Your Advisor: Steering Black-Box LLMs with Advisor Models
papers.one_line_summary: Proposes using small 'advisor' models to steer the outputs of large black-box LLMs toward user preferences without requiring access to the base model's weights or training pipeline. Demonstrates that advisor-guided generation can personalize LLM responses effectively from minimal interaction data, enabling cheap personalization of closed-source models like GPT-4.

papers.title: BARE: Combining Base and Instruction-Tuned Language Models for Better Synthetic Data Generation
papers.one_line_summary: Shows that combining outputs from both base and instruction-tuned language models produces higher quality and more diverse synthetic training data than using either model alone. Oral presentation at ICML DataWorld Workshop, demonstrating significant improvements in downstream task performance when training on BARE-generated data.

papers.title: Accelerating Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Serving with Speculation
papers.one_line_summary: Introduces a speculative execution framework for RAG systems that speculatively retrieves and processes documents in parallel before the retrieval decision is finalized, reducing end-to-end latency significantly. Published at ICML 2024, showing up to 2x speedup on RAG workloads without sacrificing output quality.
